analysis.title: Tech now accounts for two-thirds of the US trade deficit
key_insights: The US trade deficit was $105bn in September 2026, of which $64bn came from computers, peripherals and semiconductors.
US imports of tech products destined for data centres rose from about $20bn per month less than two years ago to $87bn in September, a near-vertical increase.
Much of the value added in the AI and data centre investment build is sourced overseas, so tech capex adds to GDP while tech imports subtract from it through net exports.
US imports from Korea are up 35% and from Taiwan up 60%, so money is flowing to those economies.
Net exports are a significant drag on year-on-year US GDP growth because of the tech trade deficit. Part of the imported tech ended up in inventory building, to be used in coming quarters.
The US was a net exporter of tech products only three years ago.

tension_points.theme: AI capex contribution to US GDP
tension_points.bull_case: Tech, AI token spending and data centre building add to year-on-year US GDP growth, and imported tech partly went into inventories to be used in coming quarters.
tension_points.bear_case: Much of the value added comes from overseas, and the $64bn monthly tech deficit makes net exports a significant drag on growth, offsetting the capex boost.
